In what song did Dylan say:  "You don't need to be a Weatherman
to know which way the wind blows."  (and is the wording correct?)

	And when the person indicted for a bombing turns out to 
be a right  winger -- e.g., Timothy McVeigh re Oklahoma City --
 the establishment media indicts the entire conservative movement, recklessly
casting blame on "talk radio" and the "Michigan Militia"
 which had nothing to do with the bombing.
	But when the person accused of the bombings turns out to 
be a left  wing environmentalist wacko from UC Berkeley and
 Harvard -- e .g., Ted  Kaczynski -- the mainstream media treats
 him as some sort of aberration from true liberal sentiments who
 cannot be used to blacken the name of the environmental movement.
		Jerry Desmond
		in alt.fan.unabomber

	"I would also like to kill a Communist."
		Journal entry by Ted Kaczynski

 must take a resolutely anti-leftist stance and must avoid all 
collaboration with leftists.  Leftism is in the long run inconsistent with 
wild nature, with human freedom and with the elimination of modern technology. 

		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 214)

renegade, not cozy up to him and laud his brutal anti-social

regrettable quirk in an otherwise admirable intellectual.  They were

 "leftist" background and that his brother always had problems with
 them  about their views.
		FBI interview of Anthony P. Bisceglie on January 31, 1996

	Isnï¿½t it puzzling that lately the ï¿½Lï¿½ word is used so pejoratively? 
 That the word ï¿½liberalï¿½ is used to evoke something bad?  Here are
 some things that the liberals have given us: Social Security, later 
the Social Security COLAS, federal deposit insurance, unemployment insurance,
the right to join or not to join a union, the G.I. Bill (giving educational
opportunities to veterans), Medicare and student loans for education.
	By what twist of the imagination can anyone call the above bad? 
 Let us treat the word ï¿½liberalï¿½ with the respect it deserves.
		October 17, 1988 Letter to the Editor in the Chicago Tribune,
 by Ted Kaczynskiï¿½s father, (Ted Sr.)

 of radical individualism and the tyranny that is the goal of radical
egalitarianism.
		Robert H. Bork, Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern
 Liberalism and American Decline (1996)

	The conservatives are fools:  They whine about the decay o
f traditional values, yet they enthusiastically support technological 
progress and economic growth.  Apparently it never occurs to them
 that you can't make rapid, drastic changes in the technology and the economy
of a society without causing rapid changes in all other aspects
 of the society as well, and that such rapid changes inevitably break down.  
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 50)
__________________________________________________
	Leftists, especially those of the oversocialized type, are True 
Believers in the sense of Eric Hoffer's book, The True Believer.  But 
not all True Believers are of the same psychological type as leftists.  
Presumably a true-believing nazi, for instance, is very different
psychologically from a true-believing leftist.  Because of their capacity 
for single-minded devotion to a cause, True Believers are a useful,
 perhaps a necessary, ingredient of any revolutionary movement.   
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½ (para. 222)

	Kaczynski believes "True Believers" -- of the neo-Nazi stripe -- may be a
necessary part of any revolution though he thinks that they must remain focused
on the idea of destroying technology. (para. 222)   He insists that
 his supporters not collaborate with leftists (para. 214) and only wants the
support of those members of EF!, for example, who are "thoroughly 
un-leftist." (para. 227) 
		pokerbuddy
		in newyorktimes.com forum

	The ideology of a violent Luddite would have inextricable links with
neo-nazism, the survivalist movement and common law ideology.  
The UB's ideology is *not* HD Thoreau -- although it's interesting to 
note the sympathy HD had for John Brown and violent abolitionism
 even as he sat out the Mexican American war. 
		Bobmckeown
		in newyorktimes.com forum

 many weak ass rightists as well.  I believe [he] has a much deeper
understanding of our True human natures than the vast majority of 
people, and [that] understanding, along with his far-sightedness, 
 lead him to write his/F.C.'s  manifesto.  
		Dannie Hawkins
		of W.A.R.

environmental tradition among Nazis.  You might also see the inaugural
issue of Tom Metzger's W.A.R. newspaper in October 1993, or the essay 
"We are the real greens" by Milton Kleim (a [former] member of the
 National Alliance).

Who said it ...
The Unabomber or Al Gore?

	Whenever any technology is used to mediate our experience of the world, we
gain power but we also lose something in the process. The increased
productivity of assembly lines in factories, for examples, 
requires many employees to repeat the identical task over and over 
until they lose any feeling of connection to the creative process -- and 
with it their sense of purpose.
	You said: Unabomber
	Correct answer was: Al Gore
		Web-posted quiz based on a column by Tony Snow for
 the Detroit News

 pseudo posturing and rationale.

	Statements we made in our letters to associate us with anarchism and radical
environmentalism, and therefore might make the public think of anarchists and
radical environmentalists as terrorists. So we want to 
make it clear that there is a NONVIOLENT anarchist movement that 
probably includes most people in America today who would describe 
themselves as anarchists.
	It's a safe bet that practically all of them strongly disapprove of our
bombings.  Many radical environmentalists do engage in sabotage,
 but the  overwhelming majority of them are opposed to violence against human 
beings.
	Letter from ï¿½FCï¿½ to New York Times dated June 24, 1995

because of all those right-wing bombings and shootings?

radical environmentalism) seem to include both personalities of the leftist
type and personalities of thoroughly un-leftist types who ought to know better
than to collaborate with leftists.
		Industrial Society And Its Future, by ï¿½FCï¿½  (para. 227)

	This bomber reminds me of the Weathermen from years past.  When they gave up
hope of persuading the American people of the rightness of their cause, they
resorted to terrorism out of frustration.  They hoped that their bombs would
spark some kind of uprising.  The Unabomber is to the 
green movement as the Weathermen were to the antiwar movement.  
As the spectacle of mainstream environmentalism's accommodation 
with capitalist America continues to mount, many "deep ecologists" 
will lash out in frustration. 
		Louis N Proyect
		in misc.activism.progressive

 that he would likely relate to.
		Jack Baud
		rec.radio.shortwave
__________________________________________________________
	Where I draw the line is placing him in the tradition of pure Luddites,
 who tend to be pacifists or religiously motivated or at least spiritual.  The
radical engagement with the forces of destruction ala, say, Greenpeace, tends
to be self-sacrificing.  One lays oneself on the line in the battle. 
 This is where TK balks that tradition.   The profound individualism of 
TK's ideas are what I find so disturbing, and also what link them to a
 rightist rather than environmentalist tradition.
		Bobmckeown
		in newyorktimes.com forum
